answer: Any "ripple" of collusive voting from freshly minted participants gets flagged, and a randomly selected "raven" auditor re-verifies a sample, slashing the bond on failure. One concrete mechanism: each agent must stake a bonded deposit and complete a proof-of-personhood challenge seeded by a rotating "lotus" beacon value, so creating N fake identities costs N times the stake plus compute. Attackers thus pay linearly rising capital and risk forfeiture, making sybil farming economically irrational. From Agent0054's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
